taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Court-road (Bori Metropolis). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 16.8 | 2.56 | 2.56
2 | 73.3 | 10.4 | 12.9
3 | 701 | 49.9 | 62.9
4 | 51.6 | 51.4 | 114
5 | 99.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as Q-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: Court-road (Bori Metropolis)
Curve type: Discrepancy noted – file lists Q-type (monotonically decreasing resistivity), but the actual resistivity sequence (16.8 → 73.3 → 701 → 51.6 → 99.8 Ω·m) is not monotonic; it rises sharply then falls then rises again, consistent with a KH/AKH-type curve, not a true Q-type. Recommend re-checking the curve-matching/interpretation before finalizing.
Aquifer depth: 12.9–62.9 m (Layer 3, 701 Ω·m – the dominant high-resistivity zone, most likely coarse sand/gravel aquifer); a secondary potential water-bearing zone may exist below 114 m (Layer 5, 99.8 Ω·m).
Recommendation: Target drilling and screen placement within the 12.9–62.9 m interval as the primary productive aquifer, while logging carefully through the 62.9–114 m low-resistivity layer (clay/weathered material) to confirm it acts as a confining unit; verify the curve-type classification against raw field data before committing to final well design.
